parts.title: Getting started
parts.text: Create an account, sign in on any device, and pick the Parley app that suits you. Parley is a place to talk with friends and communities: text chat, voice and video calls, live stages and a music studio. Everything is free for everyone.

parts.title: Try it without an account
parts.text: Want a look first? Open app.runparley.com/try, or click Try it without an account on the login page. You get a guest pass straight into a demo server. A guest account is removed an hour after you leave. To keep it, click Sign up to keep it in the banner. Your messages, profile and servers come with you.

parts.title: Creating an account
parts.text: 1. Go to app.runparley.com/register. 2. Enter your email and choose a username: 2 to 32 letters, numbers, _ or .. People can find you by it. 3. Optionally add a display name. This is the name people see, and it can have spaces and capitals. 4. Choose a password of at least 8 characters, then click Continue. If the people who run your Parley publish their Terms and Community Guidelines, links to them are under the form. Creating an account means you agree to them. Parley doesn't ask for your date of birth. Some places are open only to people confirmed as adults; see Your age. Parley emails you a link to verify your address. Until you click it, you can chat, but you can't create servers or use Discover. If the email didn't arrive, use Resend in the banner at the top of the app.

parts.title: Signing in
parts.text: You can sign in with any of these: - Email or username and password. - A passkey: your fingerprint, face or device PIN, with no password to type. Add one in User Settings → Account. - A QR code. On a computer, the login page shows a code. Scan it with a phone where you're already signed in, and confirm with Yes, log in. Heads up: Only scan a Parley login code that you can see on your own screen. Never scan one that someone sent you. That would sign them in as you. If you turned on two-factor authentication, Parley also asks for the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, a backup code, or your security key. Forgot your password? Click Forgot your password? on the login page and Parley emails you a link to choose a new one. More than one account? Click your picture, then Switch Accounts, to add another and flip between them.

parts.title: Getting Parley on your devices
parts.text: Where How ------ Web browser Go to app.runparley.com. Nothing to install. You can also add it to your home screen or dock with Install app in User Settings. Windows, macOS, Linux Download the desktop app from runparley.com. It runs in the background, keeps push-to-talk working while you're in a game, and has an in-game overlay. Android Install the app from runparley.com for push notifications and calls that keep going with the screen off. iPhone and iPad Use app.runparley.com in Safari, and Add to Home Screen for notifications. The desktop app updates itself. When an update is ready, a green arrow appears; click Restart to update. Note: Parley is open source, and anyone can run their own Parley server. The apps ask which server to connect to: choose app.runparley.com, or type your community's own address. Switch later with Switch server in User Settings.

parts.title: Next steps
parts.text: - Find your way around the Parley window. - Join a server or start your own. - Set up your profile so friends recognise you.

parts.title: Taking a break, or leaving
parts.text: In User Settings → Account, under Account Removal: - Disable Account logs you out everywhere and hides your account. Nothing is deleted. Log in again whenever you like to turn it back on. - Delete Account removes it for good. Before you can delete it, you'll be asked to hand over or delete any servers and apps you own. Then confirm with your password. After you delete it, you have 14 days to change your mind: just log in and choose Restore my account. After that, your personal details are erased. Your old messages stay where they are, but they're shown as from Deleted User. You can also delete your account from app.runparley.com/delete-account without opening the app.

parts.title: Finding your way around
parts.text: The parts of the Parley window, server folders, the quick switcher and search.

parts.title: The window at a glance
parts.text: From left to right: 1. The server list. At the top is Direct Messages, your private conversations and friends. Below it are your servers. At the bottom are Add a Server (+) and Discover (the compass). 2. The channel list for the server you're in. The server's name and banner are at the top; click the name for the server menu. Your own panel sits at the very bottom. 3. The conversation. Messages, with the message box underneath. The bar across the top has the channel name and buttons for threads, pins, the member list, search and your inbox. 4. The member list. Everyone who can see the channel, grouped by role, then online and offline. Click anyone to see their profile. Tip: Short on space? Hide the member list with the people button in the top bar, or with <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdU</kbd.

parts.title: Your panel
parts.text: The bottom-left corner is you. The microphone and headphones buttons mute and deafen you. The small arrow beside each one picks your microphone or speakers. The cog opens User Settings. Click your picture to: - set your status: Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb or Invisible, for good or for a while - Set a custom status: an emoji and a short line that everyone sees - Edit Profile - Switch Accounts if you use more than one While you're in a call, a Voice Connected card sits just above your panel, with the call's controls. See Voice and video.

parts.title: Server folders
parts.text: A long server list is easier to manage in folders: - Drag one server onto another to make a folder. - Drag more servers in, or drag them back out. - Click a folder to open or close it. A closed folder shows small previews of what's inside. - Right-click a folder and choose Folder Settings to name it, give it a colour or remove it. You can also right-click any server and use Add to Folder, Move Up and Move Down. Your layout is saved to your account, so it follows you to every device.

parts.title: Right-click menus
parts.text: Almost everything has a menu. Right-click it, or press and hold on a phone: - A server: Mark As Read, Invite People, notification settings, Server Settings, Leave Server. - A channel: Mark As Read, Pin Channel (keeps it at the top of the list), Invite People, Copy Link, mute and notification settings. - A category: collapse or expand it, or all of them at once. - A person: Profile, Message, Call, Add Friend, Invite to Server, Block, Report User. - A message: see Messages.

parts.title: The quick switcher
parts.text: Press <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdK</kbd (<kbd⌘</kbd+<kbdK</kbd on a Mac) and start typing the name of any server, channel or person. Press <kbdEnter</kbd to go there. Before you type, it lists your unread and recent places.

parts.title: Searching messages
parts.text: Type in the search box at the top right and press <kbdEnter</kbd. Results open in a panel beside the chat. Click Jump on any result to see it in its conversation. - Choose where to search: This channel, This server or Everywhere (your DMs included). - Sort by Most relevant, Newest or Oldest. - Narrow it down with filters. The search box suggests them as you type: Filter Finds messages… ------ from: sent by someone mentions: that mention someone in: in a channel has: with a link, embed, image, video, file, sticker, poll or sound before: during: after: from around a date pinned:true that are pinned To go back to a particular day, use the calendar button in the top bar, or <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdJ</kbd. When you've scrolled far back, Jump to Present brings you back to the newest messages. The words you searched for are marked in each result. If a search can't be run, the panel says so and offers Try again. On a phone the results fill the screen.

parts.title: On a phone
parts.text: Parley on a phone shows one thing at a time: - Swipe right for the server and channel lists. - Swipe left for the member list. - Every screen has a back button at the top. - Press and hold anything to get the menu you'd get from right-clicking on a computer.

parts.title: The getting started checklist
parts.text: New accounts see a short checklist: add a profile picture, add a friend, join or create a server, set a custom status, and add a passkey or turn on two-factor authentication (either one ticks it off). Each item takes you to the right place. Dismiss it whenever you like.

parts.title: Getting help
parts.text: This guide is always one click away: - Help & Guide in the menu under your picture, and at the bottom of User Settings, opens the guide's front page. - Every page of User Settings, Server Settings and Channel Settings has a Help button at the top. It opens the part of the guide about that page. - The keyboard shortcuts sheet (<kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbd/</kbd) links to Keyboard shortcuts.

parts.title: Joining and creating servers
parts.text: Join with an invite, find communities in Discover, or start a server of your own. A server is a community's home: its channels, its members and their roles. You can be in as many as you like.

parts.title: Joining with an invite
parts.text: Someone sends you an invite link, such as app.runparley.com/invite/parley. Open it to see the server's name, icon and how many people are there, then click Accept Invite. - No account yet? The invite page signs you up first, then brings you straight in. Some servers let you read a preview before you join. - Invite pasted in a chat? It shows as a card with a Join button. - Got just the code? Click Add a Server (+) in the server list, then Join a Server, and paste the link or code. If an invite doesn't work, it may have expired or been used up, or the server may have paused new members for now. Ask for a new one.

parts.title: Finding servers in Discover
parts.text: Click the compass at the bottom of the server list: - Home shows featured servers and lets you browse by category. - Servers lets you search everything that's listed publicly. - Stages shows live stage events you can drop in on and listen to. Click a server to look around in preview mode. You can read its public channels before you commit. When you're ready, click Join in the bar at the top. Some servers have a directory channel listing other servers you can join, such as a school's club servers.

parts.title: Your first minutes in a server
parts.text: Servers can ask a few things of new members: - Onboarding questions. Pick what you're interested in, and the server shows you the right channels and gives you matching roles. You can usually skip. - A welcome screen suggesting where to start. - Rules to accept. Until you click I agree, a bar above the message box offers View rules. - Safety checks. Some servers want a verified email, or ask newcomers to wait a few minutes before posting. The message box says what's needed.

parts.title: Creating your own server
parts.text: 1. Click Add a Server (+) at the bottom of the server list. 2. Choose how to start: - Create My Own: an empty server. - Use a Template: copy the setup of an existing server, from Parley or Discord. See Starting from a template. - Start from a template: Gaming, Friends, Study Group, School Club, Local Community or Artists & Creators. Each comes with sensible text and voice channels. 3. Give it a name and an icon, then click Create. Now invite people. Click the server name, then Invite People. To set it up properly, see Server settings.

parts.title: Starting from a template
parts.text: A server template copies a server's setup into a new server of your own: its roles, categories, channels, permissions and a few settings. Messages, members and emoji never come along. Click Add a Server (+), then Use a Template, and give it any of these: - A Parley template link, like app.runparley.com/template/…. It can be from this Parley server or from another one. - A template file (.json): click Choose a file, or drop the file onto the dialog. - A Discord template link (discord.new/…), or its code. Parley shows what the template brings first: its channels and roles. Name your server, pick an icon and click Create Server. Tip: Moving a community from Discord? In Discord, open Server Settings → Server Template, click Generate Template and copy the link. Paste it here. To share your own server's setup, see Server templates.

parts.title: Leaving a server
parts.text: Right-click the server and choose Leave Server. Your messages stay. You can come back with a new invite, unless you were banned.

parts.title: Channels, threads and forums
parts.text: The kinds of channel, threads for side conversations, forums, communities and events. Every server is split into channels, each for one topic or activity. Channels are grouped under collapsible categories.

parts.title: Kinds of channel
parts.text: Icon Kind What it's for --------- Text The everyday chat: messages, pictures, GIFs, links. 📢 Announcement Important news. Other servers can Follow it to get the posts in a channel of their own. 🔊 Voice Drop in and talk, with video and screen sharing. Each one has its own text chat too. 🎙 Stage Talks and events: a few speakers, everyone else listens and can raise a hand. 💬 Forum Organised posts with titles and tags instead of one running chat. 🖼 Media A forum where every post leads with a picture or video, shown as a gallery. 📚 Directory A list of other servers members can browse and join. 🎚 Recording Studio Make music together. See Studio. A small lock on a channel means it's private: only some roles or people can see it. Some channels show a notice before you go in: - Age-restricted channels are only for people confirmed as 18 or older. If you are confirmed, you get a warning once and then go in. If you are not, the channel shows a lock with the ways to be confirmed. See Your age. - Spoiler channels keep pictures and videos hidden until you click them. - Slowmode channels let each person post only every so often. The message box tells you how long to wait.

parts.title: Choosing which channels you see
parts.text: Big servers can be a lot. Open the server menu (click the server name) and choose Browse Channels. Tick the channels you want in your list and untick the rest. Servers may also offer roles you can pick yourself there. Other tidy-ups: - Pin Channel (right-click a channel) keeps it at the top of the list. - Hide Muted Channels (server menu) takes muted channels out of the list. - Right-click a category to collapse it, or all of them.

parts.title: Threads
parts.text: A thread is a side conversation that branches off one message, so the main channel stays readable. - Start one from a message's menu with Create Thread, or with the Threads button in the top bar. Give it a name and choose when it hides after going quiet (1 hour to 1 week). - Private Thread keeps it to the people you add (and moderators). - A thread shows as a card under its first message. Click View Thread to open it beside the chat. - Join a thread to follow it and get its notifications. Leave it to stop. - Whoever started a thread can close, archive or lock it. Show archived in the Threads list finds old ones.

parts.title: Forums
parts.text: A forum channel is a list of posts, like a message board. Each post is its own thread. - Click New Post and give it a title, a message, any tags, and files if you want. - Switch between List and Gallery, sort by Latest activity or Newest posts, and filter by tag. - Search posts finds posts by title. - Read the Post guidelines if the forum has them. Some forums require a tag on every post.

parts.title: Announcement channels
parts.text: Posts in an announcement channel can be Published from the message menu. That sends them to every channel following it, even in other servers. To get a server's announcements in your own server, click Follow in the channel's top bar. Then pick your server and channel. You need permission to manage channels in your server.

parts.title: Communities
parts.text: Very large servers can be organised into communities: groups of channels with their own page, header image and managers. - Browse Communities in the channel list shows them all. Click Follow on the ones you care about. - Following decides what shows in your channel list and what counts as unread. It doesn't change what you're allowed to see. - Click a community's name to open its page: what it's about, links, channels and who runs it. Admins: Community managers edit the page with Edit: the header image, icon, description and links. The header has its own layout editor (Adjust) with Fill or Fit, alignment and zoom. It previews on a phone, a laptop and a wide screen, because the header stretches the width of the window.

parts.title: Events
parts.text: The Events row above the channels lists the server's upcoming events. Live ones say Happening now. Click Interested to RSVP, and Parley reminds you 10 minutes before the start.

parts.title: Messages
parts.text: Write, format, mention, react, reply, attach files, run polls, schedule and bookmark messages.

parts.title: Sending a message
parts.text: Type in the box at the bottom and press <kbdEnter</kbd. For a new line without sending, press <kbdShift</kbd+<kbdEnter</kbd. - Made a typo? Press <kbd↑</kbd in an empty box to edit your last message. - Half-written messages are kept for each channel. Come back later and your draft is still there. - A message can be up to 2,000 characters. Anything longer can be sent as a file with one click.

parts.title: Formatting
parts.text: Select some text to get a small toolbar: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code and spoiler. Or type the formatting yourself: Type this To get ------ bold bold italic italic __underline__ underlined text ~~strike~~ struck-through text code code \\spoiler\\ text hidden until clicked Big heading (also , ) a heading - small print small grey text quote a quote ( quotes everything after it) - item or 1. item a list text a link with your own text For a block of code, put three backticks on the line before and the line after. Add a language name after the first three ( python ) for colours. Code blocks get a Copy button. Keyboard shortcuts work too: <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdB</kbd bold, <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdI</kbd italic, <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdU</kbd underline, <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdE</kbd code.

parts.title: Mentions
parts.text: - Type @ and a name to mention someone. They get a notification and the message is highlighted for them. - @ also finds roles, plus @everyone (everyone in the channel) and @here (everyone online). Servers decide who may use those. - Type to link a channel. Use <kbd↑</kbd and <kbd↓</kbd to pick from the suggestions, and <kbdEnter</kbd or <kbdTab</kbd to choose.

parts.title: Emoji, stickers and GIFs
parts.text: The three buttons at the right of the message box open the GIF, Sticker and Emoji pickers. - Emoji: search, your frequently used ones, every server's custom emoji, and a skin tone choice. Or type : and a name, like :tada, and pick from the list. - Parley draws emoji in one style on every device, so everyone sees the same thing, flags included, even where the computer's own emoji are out of date. - Custom emoji from any of your servers work everywhere you can post. Click one in a message to see where it's from. - Stickers come from your servers. - GIFs: search, trending and categories. Hover a GIF and click the star to keep it in Favorites.

parts.title: Reactions
parts.text: Hover a message and pick from your most-used emoji, or click Add Reaction for the full picker. Add Super Reaction adds an animated one. Click a reaction under a message to add yours, and click again to take it back. Hover a reaction to see who reacted, or choose View Reactions from the message menu.

parts.title: Replying, editing and deleting
parts.text: - Reply quotes the original above your message and notifies its author. Press <kbdEsc</kbd to cancel. - Edit Message changes what you wrote. Edited messages say (edited). Click that to see earlier versions. - Delete Message removes it for everyone. Click the quoted line above a reply to see the message it answers. Back in the bar at the bottom, or <kbdEsc</kbd, returns you to where you were.

parts.title: The message menu
parts.text: Right-click a message, click its ⋯ button, or press and hold it on a phone. You'll find: - Reply, Forward, Create Thread - Copy Text and Copy Message Link - Pin Message. Pins are listed under the pin button in the top bar (<kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdP</kbd). - Bookmark Message: save it for later in your inbox - Remind Me: in 20 minutes, an hour, 3 hours, tomorrow or next week - Mark Unread: come back to it later - Translate, if the server offers it, and Speak Message to hear it read aloud - Remove Embeds, to hide a link preview - Report Message, for anything that breaks the rules

parts.title: Files, pictures and videos
parts.text: Click + and Upload a File, drag files onto the chat, or paste them. - Up to 10 files per message, normally 25 MB each. Your server's host may allow more. - Before sending, you can Mark as spoiler or Add alt text: a description for people who use screen readers. - Pictures open full size when clicked. Videos and audio play right in the chat. - Copy Link on a file gives a link that works for a day or two, then stops, so a file from a private conversation doesn't stay open to anyone who has the link. To share a file for longer, forward the message or send the file again.

parts.title: Voice messages
parts.text: Click + and Record Voice Message. Talk, then send it or throw it away. Listeners can speed it up to 1.5× or 2×. If the server has transcripts turned on, they can also read it.

parts.title: Polls
parts.text: Click + and Create Poll: 1. Write a question and 2 to 10 answers. Each answer can have an emoji. 2. Choose whether people can pick more than one answer. 3. Choose how long it runs, from 1 hour to a week, or with no end. 4. Click Post Poll. Results update live. Whoever made the poll can close it early.

parts.title: Scheduling a message
parts.text: Write your message, then right-click the Send button (on a phone, press and hold it) and choose Schedule Message. Pick a time like Tomorrow morning, or choose Custom. You can have up to 30 scheduled messages. Find them under Scheduled in your inbox, where you can Send Now, edit or delete them.

parts.title: Forwarding
parts.text: Forward sends a copy of a message to other channels or people. It's labelled Forwarded and stays even if the original is deleted.

parts.title: Slash commands
parts.text: Type / at the start of the box to see the commands you can use: Command Does ------ /shrug /tableflip /unflip /lenny Adds the face to your message /me Sends your message in italics, as an action /spoiler Hides your whole message until clicked /tts Reads your message aloud to everyone viewing the channel /nick Changes your nickname in this server Apps and bots in the server add commands of their own. See Apps and bots.

parts.title: Summaries
parts.text: Busy channel? The Summaries button in the top bar gives a quick summary of the last couple of days. Summaries are written automatically, so check the original messages before relying on them. Servers can turn this off.

parts.title: Friends and direct messages
parts.text: Add friends, chat one-on-one or in small groups, and handle message requests. Click Direct Messages at the top of the server list to see your friends and private conversations.

parts.title: Adding friends
parts.text: 1. Click Friends, then Add Friend. 2. Type their exact username. You can add a short note so they know who you are. 3. They'll see your request under Pending and can accept it. You can also right-click anyone, or open their profile, and choose Add Friend. The friends list has tabs for Online, All, Pending and Blocked. Active Now shows friends who are in a call or streaming. For each friend you can: - Message or Wave - Notify When Online, to get a heads-up when they come online - Remove Friend or Block On anyone's profile you can set a friend nickname and a note. Only you see them.

parts.title: Direct messages
parts.text: Click a friend and Message, or use + beside Direct Messages to start a new conversation. The top bar of a DM has: - Start Voice Call and Start Video Call. See Voice and video. - Pinned Messages, Search, and the other person's profile on the right Right-click a conversation to Pin Conversation (it stays at the top), mute it, or Close DM. Closing just hides it until there's a new message.

parts.title: Group DMs
parts.text: A group DM is a small private chat for up to 10 people, with no server needed. - Start one with + and Create a group DM, then pick friends. - Add more people later with Add Friends to Group in the top bar, or share an invite link that lasts 24 hours. - Anyone can rename the group or change its icon. The owner can remove people and hand over ownership. - Calling a group rings everyone, so Parley checks with you first.

parts.title: Message requests
parts.text: Messages from people who aren't your friends go to Message Requests, so strangers can't land straight in your DMs. For each request, choose Accept, Ignore or Block. Messages that look like spam are kept separately under Spam. If one is fine, mark it Not spam. Until you are confirmed as an adult, a request shows only its text. Pictures, files and link previews stay hidden until you Accept, and you can't turn message requests off. See Your age. Choose who can message you in User Settings → Content & Social. See Settings.

parts.title: Blocking
parts.text: Block someone from their profile or by right-clicking them: - They can't message you, and you can't message them. - Their messages in shared servers collapse into blocked message. You can still click Show to read one. To undo it, use Unblock in the Blocked tab of your friends list.

parts.title: When a message can't be delivered
parts.text: If a message can't be delivered (say they only accept DMs from friends), it stays red in the chat with Retry and Delete. Parley's helper explains why.

parts.title: Voice and video
parts.text: Join voice channels, call friends, share your screen, run stages and keep calls private.

parts.title: Joining a voice channel
parts.text: Click a voice channel (the 🔊 ones), then Join Voice. You'll see who's there. Their picture lights up green when they talk. The Voice Connected card above your panel shows you're in. From it you can: - check the connection quality - turn noise suppression on or off - disconnect You can keep chatting in text channels while you're in voice. If you wander off, a small call window follows you; click Back to the call to return. Tip: The first time, Parley asks your browser for the microphone. If nobody can hear you, check User Settings → Voice & Video and try the Mic Test. You can drag the small call window to any corner and resize it from the grip on its corner; Parley remembers both. Point at it for Mute, Stop Watching and Disconnect. It also shows while you share your screen, with what you're sharing and how many people are watching. To turn it off, switch off Float the call in a corner while I look elsewhere in User Settings → Voice & Video. The channel name on the Voice Connected card also takes you back to the call.

parts.title: The call controls
parts.text: Button Does ------ Mute Turns your microphone off. The arrow beside it picks your microphone, speakers and volumes. Camera Turns your camera on. The arrow lets you preview it and pick which camera. Share Your Screen Shows a window, a tab or your whole screen. Reaction Floats an emoji over the call. Captions Live subtitles of what people say, if the server has them. Activities Watch Together (YouTube in sync), games such as Tic-Tac-Toe, and apps. Soundboard Plays one of the server's short sounds to everyone. More Grid view, whether to show your own camera and people without video. Disconnect Leaves the call. Click someone's video to focus on it, and double-click for full screen. When someone shares their screen, click Watch Stream to see it, and zoom in to read small text. Deafen (the headphones in your panel) mutes everything you hear, and your microphone with it. Everyone's picture is sized to fit the window, so there is nothing to scroll. When there are more people than fit, Parley shows those that fit and a +N tile; click it to Show everyone. Full screen shows the whole call with its controls. They fade when you stop moving the mouse and return when you move it; press <kbdEsc</k

parts.title: Calling someone
parts.text: In a DM or group DM, click Start Voice Call or Start Video Call in the top bar. The other person sees an incoming call with Join and Decline. If they miss it, they'll see that you called. You can also bring a friend into a voice channel you're in: Invite to Voice sends them a message with Join. You can answer from the keyboard: <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdEnter</kbd joins and <kbdEsc</kbd ignores. Ignore stops the ringing for you without telling the caller; Decline tells them. If you're already in the call on another device, the DM shows Join on this device.

parts.title: If a call drops
parts.text: If your connection wobbles, the call shows Reconnecting… and Parley gets you back in by itself. If it can't after a few tries, you leave the call and a Call connection failed card appears above your panel. Click Try again to rejoin, or Dismiss. Parley also tells you when something changes during a call: - No microphone: your microphone was unplugged. If you have another one, Parley switches to it and says so. If not, connect one and Parley picks it up. - New audio device: you plugged in a headset or microphone. Click Switch to use it, or Don't suggest this device again. - You were in a call: Parley reloaded or restarted in the middle of a call. Click Rejoin to go back. Parley never rejoins by itself. - Couldn't join the call: Parley couldn't open your microphone, and says why. Fix it and click Try again, or click Join without a microphone to listen. Tip: Can't connect on someone's picture means Parley can't reach them directly, usually because of a firewall. Ask whoever runs your Parley to set up a relay server.

parts.title: Stages
parts.text: Stages are for talks, Q&As and shows: - Speakers are on stage. Everyone else is in the audience and listens. - In the audience, click Raise Hand to ask to speak. - Moderators can Invite to speak and Move to audience. - Live stages from public servers show up in Discover → Stages.

parts.title: Private calls
parts.text: Calls in DMs can be end-to-end encrypted: only the people in the call can hear or see it, not even the server. Turn it on with the lock button in the DM's top bar. To be sure nobody is listening in, compare the Safety code shown in the call out loud. If everyone sees the same code, the call is private. Captions and clips are off in encrypted calls. In a small call Parley connects you directly to the others, which lets them see your IP address. To prevent that, turn on Hide my IP address in calls in User Settings → Voice & Video: your calls then go through your Parley's relay, if it has one.

parts.title: Sounding your best
parts.text: In User Settings → Voice & Video: - Input Mode: - Voice Activity sends when you talk. - Push to Talk sends only while you hold a key. Set the key with Record Keybind. In a browser it works only while Parley's tab is in front; the desktop app hears it anywhere. - Input Sensitivity sets how loud you need to be. Leave it on automatic unless people hear your keyboard. - Noise Suppression: Enhanced removes keyboards, fans and background chatter. It runs on your own device. - Echo Cancellation and Automatic Gain Control help on laptops and with speakers. - Test Video previews your camera. Screen share quality is here too.

parts.title: Clips
parts.text: Turn on User Settings → Clips to keep the last 15 seconds to a minute of a call. Then press Save Clip (or <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdAlt</kbd+<kbdC</kbd) to save it when something great happens.

parts.title: In-game overlay
parts.text: The desktop app can show who's talking on top of a full-screen game. Turn it on in User Settings → Advanced, and show or hide it with <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdO</kbd.

parts.title: Notifications and your inbox
parts.text: Control what pings you, catch up on unreads, mentions, bookmarks and reminders.

parts.title: Unread messages
parts.text: - A channel with new messages turns bold. - A server with new messages gets a small dot. - A red number means someone mentioned you or sent you a DM. Inside a channel, a bar at the top shows how many new messages there are, and a New line marks where they start. To clear unread marks: - Press <kbdEsc</kbd to mark the channel read, or <kbdShift</kbd+<kbdEsc</kbd for the whole server. - Or right-click a channel, server or DM and choose Mark As Read. To come back to something later, use Mark Unread on a message. In a channel with new messages, click the bar to go to the first one, or Mark As Read to go to the newest message and clear the New line. <kbdShift</kbd+<kbdPage Up</kbd goes to the oldest unread message.

parts.title: Choosing what notifies you
parts.text: Right-click a server, category, channel or DM (or use the server menu) for two choices: - Mute: for 15 minutes, 1 hour, 8 hours, 24 hours or Until I turn it back on. Muted places stop showing unread marks, but a direct mention of you still gets through. - Notification Settings: - All Messages - Only @mentions - Nothing - Use Server Default (channels only) For a whole server, open the server menu and choose Notification Settings. As well as the above, you can: - ignore @everyone, @here and role mentions - turn off highlights and new-event alerts - choose whether your phone gets push notifications for that server - set different rules for particular channels Tip: For a busy server, set the server to Only @mentions, then switch the one or two channels you really care about to All Messages.

parts.title: Your inbox
parts.text: The inbox button at the top right (<kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdI</kbd) collects everything waiting for you: Tab What's in it ------ Unreads Channels with new messages. Mark all read clears them. Mentions Every time someone mentioned you, for the last 30 days. Bookmarks Messages you saved, which you can sort into folders. Reminders Messages you asked to be reminded about. Highlights Things that stood out in your servers over the last two days. Scheduled Messages you've scheduled. Send them now, edit or delete them.

parts.title: Desktop, phone and email notifications
parts.text: In User Settings → Notifications: - Enable Desktop Notifications pops up a notice for new messages. - Push notifications on this browser keeps them coming even when Parley's tab is closed. You can reply or mark them read from the notification. - Unread Message Badge shows a count on the tab or app icon. - Notify me when someone replies to my message treats replies like mentions. - Phones: with the Parley app installed, your phone stays quiet while you're active on a computer. Send a test notification to my phones checks it's working. - Email notifications send at most one email an hour, and only while you're offline. - Sounds: choose which sounds play, and how loud. Event reminders arrive 10 minutes before events you marked Interested.

parts.title: Your profile
parts.text: Your picture, banner, name style, nameplate, decorations and effects, status, and a different look per server. Your profile is what people see when they click your name. Open the editor from your picture in the bottom-left corner, then Edit Profile. The editor shows a preview of your card as you go. Click your name, pronouns, status, picture or banner in the preview to jump straight to it. Nothing changes for anyone else until you click Save Changes.

parts.title: The basics
parts.text: Part Notes ------ Display name The name people see. Up to 32 characters. Pronouns Up to 40 characters. About Me Up to 400 characters, with formatting. Avatar PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP up to 8 MB. Animated pictures stay animated. You crop it to a circle, and Recent avatars lets you go back to an old one. Banner The wide picture at the top of your card. Cropped to 5:2. Around 1200×480 pixels works best. Profile theme Two colours that tint your card from top to bottom. Your username is different from your display name. Change it in User Settings → Account, at most once a day.

parts.title: Nameplate, decoration, effect and frame
parts.text: These add some style: - Nameplate: a background behind your name in member lists. - Avatar decoration: a ring or ornament around your picture. - Profile effect: an animation that plays over your card. - Profile frame: a border around your whole card. Click any of these tiles in the editor to open its picker: 1. Browse the grid, or search by name. None removes the one you have. 2. Hover or click an option to see it in the preview, exactly where people will see it. Decorations show at every size, nameplates in a member list, and effects and frames on your whole card. 3. Click Apply, or double-click an option. Then Save Changes to keep it. The grid keeps loading as you scroll, so you'll see everything. Built in options come with Parley; From this server are extras your Parley server's host has added.

parts.title: Display name style
parts.text: Display Name Style sets the font, an effect and colours for your name. Not sure? Try Surprise Me. In servers, a coloured role takes over your name colour. - Fonts: 14 typefaces, from Slab, Bubbly and Retro to Pixel, Medieval, Handwritten and Typewriter. They look the same on every device. Letters a font doesn't have, such as Japanese or Arabic, show in Parley's normal font. - Effects: Solid, Gradient, Neon, Toon, Pop, Gummy, Rainbow, Glitch, Wave and Chrome. Gradient and Pop take two colours, Gummy colours its letters in turn with three, and Rainbow uses five (pick a palette such as Holo, or your own). - Effects stand still until you point at the name, and play all the time on profile cards. Change that, or turn them off, in Settings → Accessibility.

parts.title: Tags and badges
parts.text: - Clan tag: 2 to 4 letters or numbers shown beside your name everywhere. - Server tag: wear the tag of a server you're in, if it has one. - House badge: join House of Ember, Tide or Grove. Click your house again to leave.

parts.title: Your status
parts.text: Click your picture in the bottom-left corner: - Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb (no notification pop-ups or sounds) or Invisible (you look offline, but can still use everything). You can pick one for a while, and Parley switches back afterwards. - Set a custom status: an emoji and up to 128 characters, cleared after a set time or kept until you clear it. Your custom status shows in a thought bubble beside your picture on your profile card. A long one shows its first two lines; hover over the bubble to read all of it. On someone else's card, hover over their bubble to answer it: - Send Reaction opens the emoji panel; the emoji you pick is sent to them. - Reply dims the card and opens a box under their status. Type your reply and press <kbdEnter</kbd, or press <kbdEsc</kbd to close it. Both arrive in your direct messages with them, under a "Replied to name's status" or "Reacted to name's status" line that quotes the status as it was then. When someone answers yours, it says "your status". If you connect Spotify (User Settings → Connections), people can see what you're listening to.

parts.title: A different profile per server
parts.text: You can look different in each server, say a work-friendly picture in one and a silly one in another. Open the server menu and choose Edit Server Profile, or use the Server Profiles tab in the editor. You can set: - Server nickname - Server avatar and Server banner - Pronouns and About me Anything you leave empty uses your main profile. You can also change just your nickname with /nick in the message box.

parts.title: Who sees your profile
parts.text: In the editor, Who can see your full profile can be Everyone or Friends only. Optional sections, such as Wishlist and Games, show only if you fill them in.

parts.title: Settings
parts.text: Account security, privacy, appearance, accessibility, language and the desktop app's options. Open User Settings with the cog beside your name in the bottom-left corner, or press <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbd,</kbd. Can't find something? Type in the search box at the top of the list. Instance admins also find Admin Console at the bottom of the list.

parts.title: Account
parts.text: - Account Info: change your display name, username or email. A new email is confirmed with a link first. - Password: change it, and optionally log out everywhere else at the same time. - Two-Factor Authentication: strongly recommended. Click Enable Two-Factor Auth, scan the code with an authenticator app, and type the 6-digit code to switch it on. - Save your backup codes somewhere safe. They get you in if you lose your phone. - Passkeys: sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN. Click Add a passkey. A passkey also counts as two-factor authentication for servers that require it of moderators. - Account Standing: whether you've broken any rules recently. Normally it says All good. If the people who run your Parley have limited your account, a notice here says until when and what you can't do meanwhile. - Age: see Your age. - Server Bans: servers that have banned you, with Appeal this ban where the server allows it. - Storage: how much of your upload space you've used. - Year in Review: your year on Parley. - Account Removal: disable or delete your account. See Getting started.

parts.title: Your age
parts.text: Parley doesn't ask for your date of birth. Until you are confirmed as an adult, it treats your account as it would a younger person's: - Age-restricted channels and adults-only servers stay closed. - Messages from people you haven't added arrive as requests, with pictures, files and link previews hidden until you accept. User Settings → My Account → Age shows where you stand and the ways your Parley offers to confirm you: - Verify with a service, if one is set up. It tells Parley only whether you're 18 or older. - Ask the staff to confirm I am an adult. They may contact you. Don't send identity documents through Parley. - I am 18 or older, where your Parley accepts your word for it. If none of these is offered, your Parley has no way to confirm ages yet. - I am under 18 marks your account as a teen's. Only friends can message you, sensitive media is blurred or blocked, and you can use Family Center. Only an administrator can undo it. - Birthday (optional) saves a day and a month, without the year. Only you can see it. Note: nobody else can see your age status.

parts.title: Data and privacy
parts.text: - Choose whether others see when you've read their DMs, when you're typing, and what you're doing (activity status). - Request all of my data prepares a download of everything Parley holds about you. It's ready within a day and kept for 7 days. - Trusted link destinations: websites you told Parley to open without asking first.

parts.title: Content and social
parts.text: - Who can send you DMs: everyone, friends and server members, or friends only. Strangers' messages go to Message Requests. - Who can send friend requests, and whether people can find you by searching. - Sensitive media: show, blur, filter or hide it. You can choose separately for DMs from friends, DMs from others, servers and age-restricted channels. - DM spam filter: how strictly to filter possible spam. - The Safety Center has tips and links for staying safe.

parts.title: Family Center
parts.text: Parents and teens can link their accounts. A parent sees which servers the teen joins, who they add as friends and who they message, but never what the messages say. The teen gets a code under Link a parent, and the parent enters it under Link a teen account. Either one can Unlink. The code comes from an account marked as under 18. See Your age.

parts.title: Devices and connections
parts.text: - Devices lists everywhere you're signed in. Log out one device, or Log out all other devices if you're worried someone else is using your account. - Connections links GitHub, Twitch, Spotify or Steam, and shows them on your profile if you want. - Authorized Apps lists apps and AI assistants you've let into your account. See Apps and bots.

parts.title: Appearance
parts.text: - Theme: Light, Ash, Dark, Onyx or Midnight. Color Themes offers ready-made colourful looks, and Custom lets you build your own. The editor checks your colours are easy to read. - Default theme in servers: use a server's own theme, or always yours. - Accent colour, chat font scaling and zoom level. - Message display: Cozy, with avatars and spacing, or Compact, with more messages on screen. Also UI density. - Role colours: show them in names, next to names, or not at all. - Sync settings across devices keeps your appearance the same everywhere.

parts.title: Accessibility
parts.text: - Reduced motion cuts animations. High contrast and Saturation help with readability. - Show on/off indicators adds ✓ and ✗ to switches, and Always underline links. - Choose when animated emoji, GIFs, stickers and fancy name styles play. - Text-to-speech rate, and the time format (12-hour or 24-hour).

parts.title: Voice, chat and notifications
parts.text: - Voice & Video: your microphone, speakers and camera, push-to-talk and noise suppression. See Voice and video. - Chat: link previews, how big pictures are shown, emoji suggestions, when spoilers are revealed, and your own animated typing indicator. - Notifications: see Notifications. - Keybinds: see Keyboard shortcuts.

parts.title: Language
parts.text: Parley speaks English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Turkish, Arabic, Japanese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified). Match system follows your device. Each language shows how much of it is translated.

parts.title: Streamer Mode
parts.text: Streaming or sharing your screen? Streamer Mode hides your personal details and invite links, and can silence sounds and notifications. The desktop app can turn it on by itself when OBS, Streamlabs or XSplit is running. Toggle it with <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdX</kbd.

parts.title: Clips
parts.text: Enable Clips to save the last moments of a call with one key. Clips are recorded on your own device, and you can download or delete them here. See Voice and video.

parts.title: Advanced
parts.text: - Developer Mode adds Copy ID to menus. Some bots ask for these IDs. - Desktop app only: - start with your computer, start minimised, close or minimise to the tray - the in-game overlay - hardware acceleration - App updates: choose the Stable channel (releases only) or Development (every new build; for the adventurous)

parts.title: Setting up a server
parts.text: Name, icon and banner, invites, channels, emoji and stickers, welcome and onboarding, templates and more. Open the server menu by clicking the server's name, then Server Settings. You only see the pages you have permission to change. The owner sees everything. It opens in the same window as User Settings; type in the search box at the top of the list to find a page.

parts.title: Name, icon and banner
parts.text: On Server Profile: - Icon: a square picture up to 8 MB. - Server name: up to 100 characters. Description: up to 300. - Server banner: the picture at the top of the channel list. It's cropped to 16:9; 1920×1080 is ideal. Animated GIF, APNG and WebP stay animated. - System messages channel: where Parley welcomes new members. Optionally it prompts members to wave hello. - Server rules: up to 4,000 characters. Tick Members must accept the rules before chatting to have newcomers agree first. - Default notification settings for new members, and whether members may schedule messages. After picking a picture, drag and zoom to frame it. To reframe it later, click Adjust. Also here: - Server Theme: give the server its own colours. Members can choose to see them. - Server Tag: a short tag and badge that members can wear beside their name. - Insights: how many people join and stay, how busy it is, and which channels are most popular.

parts.title: Inviting people
parts.text: Click Invite People in the server menu for a link to share. On Invites in Server Settings you can make custom invites: - Expire after: 30 minutes up to 30 days, or never. - Max uses: from 1 to 100, or no limit. - Grant temporary membership: people leave automatically when they log off, unless they've been given a role. Every active invite is listed, with Revoke to cancel one. Public servers listed in Discover can also have a custom vanity link. Access: to approve people by hand, turn on Review new members before they can chat and write a few questions. Applications wait for you to Approve or Reject.

parts.title: Channels and categories
parts.text: - Create Channel is in the server menu, or click + beside a category. See Channels for the kinds. - Drag channels and categories to reorder them. - Right-click a channel and choose Edit Channel for: - its topic and Slowmode - Age-Restricted and Spoiler settings. An age-restricted channel is open only to members confirmed as 18 or older; everyone else sees it locked. Turn it on for a category and every channel in it is restricted. Only someone who is confirmed themselves can turn it off again. - for voice: the user limit, video and audio quality, and end-to-end encryption - forum Tags - Permissions: see Roles and permissions

parts.title: Emoji, stickers and sounds
parts.text: Limit Files --------- Emoji 100 per server PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP under 512 KB. Names of 2 to 32 letters, numbers or _. Stickers 60 per server Under 1 MB. 320×320 pixels works best. Soundboard 48 per server MP3, OGG, WAV, WebM or M4A under 512 KB (about 5 seconds). Members can use your custom emoji in any server they're in.

parts.title: Welcoming new members
parts.text: - Welcome Screen: a greeting with up to 5 suggested channels, shown when someone joins. - Onboarding: questions for newcomers ("What brings you here?"). Each answer can give them roles and channels, so people see what's relevant. Mark questions Required, or allow several answers. - Rules: set on Server Profile. Members click I agree before they can post.

parts.title: Communities inside your server
parts.text: In a big server, group channels into communities. Each gets its own page and managers. - Create one with + beside Communities in the channel list. - Open its page and click Edit. You can set: - its icon, name and description - a web address - an About section and Links - who looks after it, and its channels - Add header image gives the page a banner: - Wide pictures of 1600 pixels or more work best. - Click Adjust to choose Fill or Fit, line it up with the alignment grid, and zoom. - Previews show how it looks on a phone, a laptop and a wide screen. - Delete community is at the top of the editing bar. It deletes the community's channels and their messages too.

parts.title: Getting found
parts.text: - Discovery: list the server in Discover with a category, a description and a banner. An admin reviews it first. - Widget: an embeddable box for your website, showing who's online with a Join button. - Badge: a live "Join us" badge for a README or website.

parts.title: Server templates
parts.text: Server Settings → Server Template shares your server's setup (its roles, categories, channels, permissions and a few settings) so others can start a server just like it. Messages, members and emoji are never copied. - Download template file saves the server as it is right now as a .json file. Keep it as a backup of your setup, or send it to someone. No link needed. - Share a link: give the template a title and description, then Generate Template. The link stays the same; click Sync Template after changing your server so the link gives the new setup. Delete Template turns the link off. Anyone can create a server from a template file or link with Add a Server → Use a Template, on any Parley server. See Starting from a template. People who open a template link see what it sets up, and can create a server from it or download it as a file.

parts.title: Handing over or closing down
parts.text: These are at the bottom of the list, for the owner only: - Transfer Ownership hands the server to another member. - Delete Server: type the server's name and your password to confirm. Changed your mind? You have 7 days to restore it from User Settings → Account.

parts.title: Roles and permissions
parts.text: Give people roles, decide who can do what, and make channels private. Roles are labels you give members, such as Moderator, Artist or New here. Each role comes with permissions that decide what its members can do. A role can also have a colour and an icon shown beside their names. Everyone in the server automatically has the @everyone role. Its permissions are what everybody can do.

parts.title: Making a role
parts.text: 1. Open Server Settings → Roles and click Create Role. 2. Give it a name and a colour. Optionally: - give it a Role icon (an emoji or a small picture) - Display role members separately in the member list - Allow anyone to @mention this role - Let members pick this role themselves 3. Switch on the permissions it should have. 4. Add people on the Members tab, or right-click someone in the member list and pick roles. Duplicate Role copies a role, which is handy for making a similar one.

parts.title: Which role wins
parts.text: Roles are listed in order, and roles higher up outrank lower ones. Drag them, or use Move up and Move down. - People can only manage roles below their own highest role. - When roles disagree about a colour, the highest role's colour is used. View Server As Role shows you exactly what a member with that role sees, so you can check your setup.

parts.title: Permissions
parts.text: Permissions are grouped: General, Membership, Text, Voice and Studio. Some that matter most: Permission Lets people… ------ Administrator Do everything, and skip every channel restriction. Give it sparingly. Manage Server Change the server's name, icon and settings. Manage Roles Create and assign roles below their own. Manage Channels Create, edit and delete channels. Kick / Ban / Timeout Members Moderate people. See Moderation. Manage Messages Delete and pin anyone's messages. Mention @everyone Ping the whole server. Create Invite Invite new people. Manage Expressions Add emoji, stickers and sounds. Manage Events Schedule events. View Audit Log See who changed what. Tip: Start with @everyone able to read and chat. Then add a Moderator role with Kick, Timeout and Manage Messages. Few people need Administrator.

parts.title: Channel permissions
parts.text: To make a channel private, or change what people can do in one channel: 1. Right-click the channel, choose Edit Channel, then Permissions. 2. Turn on Private channel to hide it from everyone except the roles and people you add. 3. Or use Add role or member and set each permission to Allow (✓), Deny (✗) or Inherit (/, the server-wide setting). Categories have permissions too. A channel that matches its category says Synced; Sync Now makes it match again after you've changed it.

parts.title: The member list
parts.text: Server Settings → Members lists everyone. Search, filter by role, see how each person joined, and give or take away roles. You can also select several people at once to kick or ban them.

parts.title: Linked roles
parts.text: A linked role is given automatically to people who've connected an account, for example Twitch subscribers. Set these up under Integrations.

parts.title: Moderation and safety
parts.text: Keep your server friendly with AutoMod, timeouts, bans, reports, raid protection and the audit log.

parts.title: Dealing with someone
parts.text: Right-click a person (or press and hold on a phone) for these options: Option What happens ------ Timeout They can read but can't post, react, or join voice for 60 seconds up to a week. Remove Timeout ends it early. Kick Removes them. They can come back with a new invite. Ban Removes them and stops them coming back. You can also delete their messages from the last few days, up to 7. Moderator View Their history in your server: warnings, timeouts and notes. You can Warn them, or Quarantine them while you look into something. Always add a reason. It's kept in the audit log, so the rest of the team knows what happened. Unban people under Server Settings → Bans. Banned members can appeal, if the server allows it. Appeals wait there for you to accept or deny. To clear a spam flood, type /purge 50 to delete the last 50 messages, or /purge 50 @someone to delete only theirs (up to 100 at a time).

parts.title: AutoMod
parts.text: Server Settings → AutoMod catches problems automatically, even when no moderator is around. Rules can: - Block words: a list of words or phrases. Use as a wildcard. - Block mention spam: messages that ping too many people at once. - Block links: links to any site except the ones you allow. - Filter nicknames that break your rules. For each rule, choose what happens: - block the message, optionally with a message of your own to the sender - send an alert to a moderators' channel - time the person out You can also exempt roles or channels, like a channel where your moderators discuss bad words. People who can manage the server are never filtered.

parts.title: Safety Setup
parts.text: Server Settings → Safety Setup has the big switches: - Verification level: what a newcomer needs before they can post. Low requires a verified email. Medium also requires a Parley account older than 5 minutes. High also requires 10 minutes in your server. Members with any role skip it. - Raid protection: notices a sudden rush of new accounts and alerts your moderators. - Pause invites and Pause DMs between members: emergency brakes during a raid. - Adults-only server: tick Everything in this server is 18+ and only members confirmed as 18 or older can read or join in, anywhere in the server. To restrict only some areas, use Age-Restricted on a channel or a category instead. See Channels and categories. - Explicit image filter: scans pictures posted in the server. Each member's app does the checking, and so does the instance if its admins have set that up. - Two-factor authentication for moderators: moderators must have 2FA turned on or a passkey added, so a stolen password can't be used against the server. Either one counts, and you need one yourself to switch this on. - AI summaries: turn the Summaries button on or off.

parts.title: Reports
parts.text: When members Report Message or Report User and tick the box to tell this server's moderators too, the report lands under Server Settings → Reports. Jump to see it in context, then Resolve or Dismiss it. Reports about a child's safety or about intimate pictures shared without consent never show up here. They go only to the team that runs your Parley server.

parts.title: The audit log
parts.text: Audit Log records who changed what: roles, channels, bans, kicks, timeouts, deleted messages and settings. Filter by person or by kind of action. It's the first place to look when something changes and nobody knows why.

parts.title: Reporting to Parley
parts.text: Some things go beyond one server, like threats, illegal content or spam across many servers. Every report goes to the admins who run your Parley server. Ticking the box also sends it to that server's moderators. To report, right-click a message and choose Report Message, or right-click a person and choose Report User. Pick what's wrong, add anything that helps, and choose Submit Report. Some reasons are looked at first: Threat of violence, Someone may hurt themselves, Intimate pictures shared without consent, and most of the choices under A child is at risk. Reports about a child's safety or about intimate pictures go only to the team that runs your Parley server, never to a server's moderators, so the box isn't offered for them. What you report is copied the moment you send it: the message, any files on it and, in a server channel, what was said just before and after. Deleting the message afterwards doesn't remove the copy. Heads up: If you come across sexual pictures or video of a child, don't save, screenshot or forward them, even as proof. Report the message and leave it there. Your report keeps what's needed. Note: If someone is in danger right now, call your local emergency n

parts.title: Apps, bots and AI assistants
parts.text: Add bots to your server, use their commands, and connect an AI assistant to your account. Apps add features to Parley. A bot is an app that joins a server like a member: it can welcome people, run games, play music or post updates.

parts.title: Finding apps
parts.text: Open the App Directory from Discover (Browse the App Directory) or from User Settings → Authorized Apps. Search or browse by category. A Verified badge means Parley has checked who made it.

parts.title: Adding a bot to your server
parts.text: 1. Click Add to Server on the app, or open the invite link its maker gives you. 2. Pick a server where you have Manage Server permission. 3. Check the permissions it asks for. Untick any it doesn't need. 4. Click Authorise. The bot gets a role of its own. You can change its permissions in Server Settings → Roles. To remove a bot, use Server Settings → Integrations, or kick it like any member.

parts.title: Apps just for you
parts.text: Some apps can be added to your own account with Add to My Apps. Then you can use them anywhere: in any server or DM. They also show up under Apps when you right-click a message or a person.

parts.title: Using commands
parts.text: Type / at the start of the message box. Parley's own commands come first, then the commands of every app you can use there. Pick one, fill in its options, and press <kbdEnter</kbd. Some apps open a form or reply only to you.

parts.title: AI assistants
parts.text: You can let an AI assistant, such as Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, read and send messages for you. Ask it things like "what did I miss?" or "reply to Sam that I'm running late". 1. Open User Settings → Authorized Apps and copy the address under AI assistants (MCP). 2. In your assistant, add it as a custom connector (it may be called a remote MCP server). 3. Parley opens a page asking what the assistant may do: Read, Notifications, Send messages or Manage servers. Pick only what you need, then approve. Heads up: Anything the assistant sends appears under your name. With Manage servers it could delete messages or remove people, so only allow that if you really mean to. To stop it, click Disconnect next to the assistant in Authorized Apps.

parts.title: Tools for admins
parts.text: Some tools that work on your instance, such as Profile Studio for making profile cosmetics, sign in the same way. When you sign in from the tool, Parley opens a page asking to let it Manage cosmetics: add cosmetics to the instance and change existing ones. It only works if your account can manage the instance, and the tool never sees your password. Heads up: Anything it adds or changes shows for everyone at once. Only allow tools you trust. To stop it, click Disconnect next to the tool in Authorized Apps.

parts.title: Making your own
parts.text: Want to build a bot? Create an app in User Settings → Applications, and read the developer docs.

parts.title: Studio
parts.text: Record, arrange and mix songs together in a Recording Studio channel, live or in your own time. A Recording Studio channel is a music workspace inside your server. Each project is a song, with its own multitrack editor, takes, comments, versions and chat. Band members can record together live, or add parts whenever they have time.

parts.title: Starting a project
parts.text: Open a Recording Studio channel and click New Project. Give it a name and a tempo. You need the Create Projects permission. Already started a song somewhere else? Import opens .dawproject files from Bitwig, Studio One, Cubase and others, as well as Parley's own .parley-project files.

parts.title: Recording
parts.text: 1. Set up your audio in the Audio panel: your output, and Recording latency. Click Measure so your takes line up with the beat. 2. Add a track: audio for a microphone or instrument, or MIDI with a built-in synth, drum kit or sampler. 3. Arm the track and press record. Record the band records everyone in the session from the playhead; Record alone records just you. A take can be up to 30 minutes. No MIDI keyboard? Play notes with your computer keys: <kbdA</kbd to <kbdK</kbd are the white notes, and <kbdZ</kbd and <kbdX</kbd change octave.

parts.title: Arranging and editing
parts.text: Keys Does ------ <kbdSpace</kbd Play or stop <kbdHome</kbd Back to the start <kbdL</kbd Loop on or off <kbdS</kbd Split the clip at the playhead <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdD</kbd Duplicate <kbdQ</kbd Quantise (snap notes to the grid) <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdZ</kbd / <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdZ</kbd Undo / redo <kbdTab</kbd Switch between the arrangement and the mixer Double-click a MIDI clip to open the piano roll. There are also a metronome and count-in, markers, tempo changes, and automation lanes for volume and effects. In the mixer, every track has volume, pan, solo, mute, effects and sends.

parts.title: Effects
parts.text: Each track, bus and the master has an effects rack: EQ, filter, compressor, gate, limiter, reverb, delay, drive and chorus. Click + Effect to add one. Effects play top to bottom; hover one to move it or remove it. Click an effect to open its window. You can open as many windows as you like and drag them anywhere; click a window to bring it to the front. Each window shows what the effect does: - EQ and filter: the frequency curve over the sound's spectrum. Drag the dots on the curve to shape it. On the filter, drag up or down for more or less resonance, or use the mouse wheel. - Compressor, gate and limiter: how loud goes in versus how loud comes out, a dot showing where your sound is now, the last few seconds of level, and how much is being turned down. - Reverb: the shape of the tail. Delay: each echo fading away. Drive: the distortion curve, with the sound before and after. Chorus: the sweep. While the song plays, the views and the In and Out meters move with the sound. To change a setting: - Drag a knob up or down. Hold <kbdShift</kbd for fine control. - Use the mouse wheel or the arrow keys. - Type a value under the knob, such as 2.5k or 25%. - Double-click a knob to put it bac

parts.title: Examples
parts.text: These start from an effect's defaults. Play the song while you work, ideally with Loop on, so the windows show your sound. Clean up the low end of a guitar or vocal. Add an EQ. Drag the C dot on the curve to the right until Low cut reads about 90 Hz; the rumble below it goes, and the spectrum behind the curve shows what you took away. Drag the M dot to about 2.5k and up a few dB to bring the part forward. Even out a vocal. Add a Compressor. Set Ratio to 4:1, then turn Threshold down while you watch the dot on the curve: when the loud words cross the bend, the GR meter shows how much they are turned down. Aim for about 3 to 6 dB on the loudest words, then raise Makeup by about the same amount so the part is as loud as before. Sweep a filter. Add a Filter to a synth or drum track and pick Low-pass. Drag the dot on the curve slowly from right to left while the song plays: the sound gets darker as the cutoff moves down. Drag the dot up or down, or scroll the mouse wheel over it, to change Resonance: more gives a sharper, ringing peak at the cutoff. To make the sweep part of the song, record it with an automation lane. Stop a noisy track hissing between notes. Add a Gate first in the ra

parts.title: Working as a band
parts.text: - Band: everyone is an Engineer (can change anything) or an Artist (records their own parts). Protect this track stops others editing your part. - Sessions: an engineer clicks Start session to work live together. Everyone hears what anyone plays. - Takes: every recording is kept. Pick the best one with Use take. - Comments: leave notes at a point in the song, like "drums drag here", and Resolve them when done. - Versions: Save version before big changes, and Restore if you don't like where it went. Listeners who aren't in the band can still play the song, follow along and comment. Lost your connection? Keep working. Your changes are saved and sent when you're back online.

parts.title: Working somewhere else
parts.text: A project keeps playing, and a take keeps recording, when you go to a chat or another channel. While it does, a card above your name at the bottom left shows the project, whether it's Playing or Recording, and the time. It also shows while you're in the project's voice room. Its row in the channel list shows moving bars while it plays and a red dot while it records. - Click the project's name on the card to go back to it. - Stop or play from the card. Play carries on from where you stopped. - Stop the take from the card, if you could stop it in the project. - Done with it? Stop it, then click ✕ to close the card.

parts.title: Sharing the result
parts.text: The Export panel can: - export the mix as WAV, FLAC or MP3 - export stems (each track separately, zipped) - Post the mix to a channel for everyone to hear - save the project as .dawproject to open in another music app

parts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
parts.text: Every shortcut, and how to change them. Press <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbd/</kbd in Parley to see this list at any time. On a Mac, use <kbd⌘</kbd wherever it says <kbdCtrl</kbd.

parts.title: Getting around
parts.text: Keys Does ------ <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdK</kbd Quick switcher: jump to any server, channel or person <kbdAlt</kbd+<kbd↑</kbd / <kbd↓</kbd Previous / next channel <kbdAlt</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbd↑</kbd / <kbd↓</kbd Previous / next unread channel <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdAlt</kbd+<kbd↑</kbd / <kbd↓</kbd Previous / next server <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdI</kbd Open your inbox <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdP</kbd Pinned messages <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdU</kbd Show or hide the member list <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdJ</kbd Jump to a date <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbd,</kbd User Settings <kbdAlt</kbd+<kbd←</kbd / <kbd→</kbd Back / forward (desktop app)

parts.title: Messages
parts.text: Keys Does ------ <kbdEnter</kbd Send <kbdShift</kbd+<kbdEnter</kbd New line <kbd↑</kbd (in an empty box) Edit your last message <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdE</kbd Go to the message box <kbdEsc</kbd Cancel a reply, or mark the channel read <kbdShift</kbd+<kbdEsc</kbd Mark the whole server read <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdB</kbd / <kbdI</kbd / <kbdU</kbd Bold / italic / underline the selection <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdS</kbd Strikethrough <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdE</kbd Code Start typing anywhere and your words go into the message box.

parts.title: Voice
parts.text: Keys Does ------ <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdM</kbd Mute or unmute <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdD</kbd Deafen or undeafen <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdAlt</kbd+<kbdC</kbd Save a clip of the call <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdX</kbd Streamer Mode on or off <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdO</kbd In-game overlay (desktop app)

parts.title: Changing shortcuts
parts.text: Open User Settings → Keybinds to change any of these, or to add a Push to Talk key. The desktop app can also listen for some shortcuts while you're in another app, such as a game.
